svg.title: Abnormal uterine bleeding divided by age: reproductive age split by the exam into structural (PALM) or functional (COEIN) causes, adolescence and perimenopause, and post-menopausal bleeding worked up in three steps to the biopsy report that picks atrophy, hyperplasia or carcinoma; each column gives clues, numbered investigations and treatment in order

svg.text: Abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB): divide by AGE first

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: any change in frequency, duration or amount of flow, or bleeding between cycles

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: every one: is she STABLE? vitals first · β-hCG (pregnant: see the FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart)

svg.text: treat the cause; otherwise regulate the bleeding: medicines → minimally

svg.text: 1 · Exam with a SPECULUM: a negative Pap test does not end it

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 2 · Transvaginal ultrasound: endometrium < 5 mm is normal

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: 3 · ENDOMETRIAL BIOPSY if > 5 mm, or bleeding recurs · HYSTEROSCOPY for a focal lesion or a failed biopsy
